title: Memorandum of the Controller's Office: Treating a Member's Equity Across Their Several Classes
content:
Equity under Membership and Patronage Equity is looked at across every membership a member holds rather than class by class. This memorandum states how business is directed to one of those memberships, how revolvement is taken across them, and what the class floors and ceilings do to the equity standing on each.

**1. Where qualifying business is allocated.** Qualifying business is allocated to the voting membership where the member holds one, and only where they hold none does it fall to the associate account; it is never split across two memberships, because the business was done once. Where a member holds a preferred membership as well, the order in which a target is sought is the voting membership first, the preferred membership next, and the associate account last.

**2. How revolvement is taken.** The member's share of the annual pool is taken across all their memberships together in the order the classes fix, so a member holding both a voting membership and a certificate holding is paid the older of the two allocation years first regardless of which membership carries it. Each class contributes its own cycle in fiscal years, its own pool percentage, its own order, its own floor and its own ceiling, as the class schedule carries them.

**3. The ceiling.** Equity on a class that has reached its maximum equity balance earns no further retention, and the equity portion of any further allocation on that class is paid in cash instead.

**4. The floor.** Equity on a class below its minimum equity balance is not revolved below that minimum while the membership stays open, since the minimum is what keeps the class alive.

## A clause of this article no longer in force

The following sentence of this article is **no longer in force** and is reproduced here only so that no reader applies it: "Revolvement is paid out of a single annual pool the board fixes as a percentage of unrevolved equity". The basis on which a year's revolvement pool is now taken is the current one and is carried with the revolvement rules themselves. The remaining clauses of this article, including the order of payment across a member's memberships and the treatment of the floor and the ceiling, stand as clauses in force.

## Points of judgement

A member holding a voting membership and an associate account does the year's grain business once; it is allocated to the voting membership, and nothing of it falls to the associate account. A member holding only an associate account has that account as the target. A member whose certificate holding carries the older allocation year is paid on that holding before the voting membership, although the voting membership is where the business was allocated.

superseded_clauses: Revolvement is paid out of a single annual pool the board fixes as a percentage of unrevolved equity
